subject: Consequence ladder & exceptions to standard SLA
messages:
From: Evan Thompson <evan.thompson@waveapps.com>

Cc: contracts@waveapps.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Consequence ladder & exceptions to standard SLA

Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team reviewed Redwood's standard SLA and sent along a set of requested exceptions (attached). High level asks: termination rights for repeated outages, a fee-at-risk arrangement or liquidated damages for severe outages, and a clearer ladder of consequences (credits -> fee at risk -> termination) tied to uptime/latency metrics.

We understand this is not standard, but WaveApps is operating a payroll product and needs stronger commercial remedies should SLA targets be missed. Can you confirm whether Redwood can:

- Accept a limited termination right after X days of unremedied outages?
- Agree to a fee-at-risk or liquidated damages bucket for material downtime (we proposed 6 months NRR in the redlines).
- Formalize a consequence ladder so that credits escalate to (b) fee, then (c) termination in specified circumstances.

We've attached our redlines (Customer_Request_Redlines.docx) and are happy to take a short call to walk through.

Regards,
Evan Thompson
Director, Platform Reliability
WaveApps

Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Consequence ladder & exceptions to standard SLA (internal)

Team — internal read before the customer call.

Summary of WaveApps asks (from Evan's redlines):
- Termination right after recurring/unremedied outages tied to uptime % over rolling 30/60/90 day windows.
- Fee-at-risk / liquidated damages up to 6 months NRR.
- Explicit ladder: 50% credit after first breach, then a fee, then termination.

Our concerns / negotiation points:
- Liquidated damages / open fee-at-risk: high legal & financial risk; precedent dangerous for existing enterprise customers.
- Termination: acceptable in a tightly-limited form (material breach after extended cure window) but must be mutual and capped.
- Credits ladder: reasonable to scale credits; operationally doable if we link to measurable incidents and provide transparency in metrics/logs.

Suggested counter (initial):
- Maintain standard credit approach but scale upwards: 10% credits for minor misses, 25% for major, 50% for sustained outage windows (define thresholds).
- Cure period: 60 to 90 days of continuous missed SLOs before termination right vests (customer may terminate for cause thereafter).
- Termination fee: capped to a fixed multiple of committed monthly spend (e.g., 2-3 months) — not open-ended "fee-at-risk" tied to future NRR.
- Reject liquidated damages language. Offer enhanced operational commitments (dedicated SRE on call for the first 90 days post-go-live) for a negotiated premium instead.

Attached is a working draft of the SLA that integrates these options (SLA_Redwood_Draft_v3.pdf).

Laura: can you weigh in from leadership—is giving a capped termination fee (2-3 months) acceptable for this tier? This is a mid-sized expansion deal; precedent matters but revenue upside is meaningful.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success (Accounts)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Redwood_Draft_v3.pdf (pdf)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Consequence ladder & exceptions to standard SLA (legal viewpoint)

Quick legal take:
- Liquidated damages: strongly advised against. Difficult to justify and enforce; likely to trigger reciprocal requests from other customers.
- Fee-at-risk: can be structured as a fixed termination fee (one-time) tied to committed spend, but not as an ongoing "at-risk" bucket we pay out procedurally. Proposed language: "Upon Customer termination for uncured material SLA breach, Customer may receive a one-time termination payment not to exceed two (2) months of Customer's committed monthly fees."
- Cure period: recommend minimum 60 days measured across rolling 90-day window to ensure we have time to remediate.
- Metrics and adjudication: require mutually agreed incident classification process and third-party audit rights only for severe outages (not routine).

If leadership is comfortable, we can present the above as Redwood's firm counter: credits + scaled remedies + capped termination payment. I can draft contract language for the DocuSign packet.

Priyom Das
Sr. Counsel (Commercial Contracts)
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evan Thompson <evan.thompson@waveapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, contracts@waveapps.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Consequence ladder & exceptions to standard SLA

Evan —

Thanks for your patience while we reviewed your redlines. I've summarized Redwood's position below so your legal team can compare line-by-line with your draft: 

1) Liquidated damages / open fee-at-risk: we cannot accept liquidated damages or an open fee-at-risk structure tied to future NRR. This exposes Redwood to unpredictable, uncapped liability and sets a precedent that would be difficult for us to maintain across our enterprise customers.

2) Service credits ladder: we will formalize an escalating credit schedule tied to measurable uptime/latency thresholds. Example: minor breach = 10% credit, major = 25%, sustained = 50% (detailed thresholds to be included in the SLA). Credits are our primary remedy and are payable as set-offs against invoices.

3) Limited termination right: we can offer a customer termination right for uncured material SLA breaches, but with controls —
   - Termination vests only after a sustained failure (e.g., 60-90 days of failing the agreed SLOs measured on a rolling basis).
   - Termination payment (if any) will be a one-time cap equal to two (2) months of the customer's committed monthly fee (not an open-ended fee-at-risk).
   - Termination must follow the agreed incident classification and adjudication process (mutual agreement + reasonable evidence).

4) Operational mitigations: for WaveApps specifically we can offer an onboarding SRE engagement for the first 90 days post-launch and prioritized incident escalation during the term.

5) Next steps: Priyom will prepare redline language for the DocuSign packet that implements the above counter. If you'd like, we can set an executive-level call (Marissa, myself and Priyom) to resolve outstanding commercial points.

If WaveApps can accept those constraints, we can move to a final DocuSign within the week. Please advise preferred times for a call.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
